title: Discretisation of quantum feedback networks for implementation on a quantum computer
abstract: Quantum Feedback Network Theory (also known colloquially as the SLH-framework) is a powerful tool for modeling systems in quantum optics. This paper describes a method for discretising SLH-networks such that they can be implemented on a quantum computer. Building on a discretisation theorem for quantum stochastic differential equations, we establish strong convergence, uniformly on compact time intervals, of the discretised system to the continuous SLH-network as the discretisation mesh goes to zero.
summary: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical framework for discretizing Quantum Feedback Networks, which are fundamental tools in quantum optics. By proving strong convergence of discrete approximations to the continuous evolution governed by QSDEs, it provides a pathway to simulate complex quantum optical systems on actual quantum computers.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a rigorous method to discretize Quantum Feedback Networks (SLH-networks) so that their time evolution can be accurately simulated on a quantum computer.
main_result: The authors establish strong convergence, uniformly on compact time intervals, showing that the discrete approximation converges to the continuous SLH-network as the discretization mesh approaches zero.
method: The work utilizes quantum stochastic calculus (Hudson-Parthasarathy) and establishes convergence by relating the discrete evolution operator to the continuous unitary co-cycle governing the network dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is based on Quantum Feedback Networks, which are described by coefficients $(S, L, H)$ derived from a quantum stochastic differential equation (QSDE). These networks are relevant for modeling complex systems in quantum optics, such as cavity QED.
key_observables: The network time evolution operator $\hat{U}_t$, and the convergence of discrete approximations $M_k(l)$ to this continuous limit.
important_parameters: The discretization mesh size ($\sigma$ or related parameters), and the structure defined by the SLH-triple $(S, L, H)$.
main_assumptions: Convergence theorems rely on assumptions regarding the boundedness of coefficients in the QSDE and the properties of cocycles.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the continuous dynamics via QSDEs to constructing a discrete approximation using recursive generators, culminating in convergence proofs based on established theorems for semigroups.
why_interesting: This work provides the necessary theoretical guarantees (strong convergence) to translate complex quantum optical models into algorithms executable on near-term quantum hardware.
